informational.title: General informational purposes only
informational.body: ImmiMap is a public directory and educational resource. All content on this website — including organization listings, maps, processing-time and visa-bulletin information, Know Your Rights materials, and related materials — is provided for general informational purposes only. Nothing on this site constitutes legal advice, a legal opinion, or a recommendation regarding any particular immigration case, application, or strategy.

noRelationship.title: No attorney-client relationship
noRelationship.body: Use of ImmiMap, including browsing listings, contacting a listed provider through information published here, or reading educational content, does not create an attorney-client, counsel, or any other professional relationship between you and ImmiMap, its operators, contributors, or any organization or individual listed on the site. A professional relationship is formed only when you and a qualified provider expressly agree to one under applicable law and professional rules.

verifyCredentials.title: Independently verify credentials
verifyCredentials.body: ImmiMap works to list organizations with publicly available or reviewed information, but listings may be incomplete, outdated, or incorrect. Before relying on any representative, you must independently verify their credentials, licensing status, scope of services, fees, languages offered, and availability. Confirm standing with the relevant state bar, the U.S. Department of Justice recognition and accreditation program (where applicable), and the organization itself.

uplWarning.title: Unauthorized practice of law (UPL) warning
uplWarning.body: Only licensed attorneys and U.S. Department of Justice (DOJ) recognized organizations / accredited representatives are authorized to provide immigration legal advice in the United States, subject to applicable law and the scope of their accreditation. Be cautious of "notarios," notary publics, immigration consultants, and other unauthorized individuals who may offer immigration advice or document preparation. Using unauthorized providers can cause serious harm, including forms submitted incorrectly, missed deadlines, loss of status, denial of benefits, removal proceedings, or fraud. If someone claims they can "fix" immigration problems for cash, demand power of attorney for improper purposes, or tells you not to deal with licensed counsel, treat that as a red flag and seek help only from a licensed attorney or DOJ-accredited representative.

liability.title: No warranties; limitation of liability
liability.body: ImmiMap is provided "as is" without warranties of any kind, express or implied, including accuracy, completeness, merchantability, or fitness for a particular purpose. To the fullest extent permitted by law, ImmiMap and its operators are not liable for any loss, damage, claim, or consequence arising from your use of the site, reliance on any listing or content, or contact with any third-party provider. Decisions about immigration matters should be made with qualified professional assistance tailored to your circumstances.

Verify.title: How we verify organizations
Verify.lead: The Verified badge marks nonprofit immigration organizations that meet ImmiMap's review standards. We publish these criteria so families and advocates can understand what the label means — and what it does not.
Verify.badgeTooltip: This nonprofit provides active immigration legal or social services and has passed ImmiMap's verification review.

criteria.title: Verification criteria
criteria.intro: An organization receives the Verified badge only when it meets all of the following standards. Law firms and private practices are listed separately and are not eligible for this badge.

nonprofit.title: Recognized nonprofit or legal aid status
nonprofit.description: The organization operates as a registered nonprofit, accredited legal aid provider, or equivalent publicly recognized immigration support entity — not as an unregulated immigration consultant or fee-for-service scam operation.

activeServices.title: Active immigration services
activeServices.description: The organization currently offers immigration legal representation, case assistance, or direct social services to immigrant communities. Defunct programs, placeholder listings, or organizations outside immigration work are not verified.

contactInfo.title: Confirmable contact details
contactInfo.description: Public contact information — including address and website — is current and matches what appears on the organization's official channels or government registries.

publicRecord.title: Alignment with public records
publicRecord.description: Listing details are cross-checked against authoritative sources such as IRS nonprofit records, state bar or legal aid directories, and Department of Justice recognition lists where applicable.

manualReview.title: Manual ImmiMap review
manualReview.description: Every Verified organization is individually reviewed by the ImmiMap team before the badge is applied. Automated data alone is not sufficient for verification.

process.title: Our review process
process.description: Verification is performed during initial cataloging and re-checked during regular data refreshes. If an organization no longer meets these standards, the Verified badge is removed until the listing is corrected or reconfirmed.

limitations.title: What Verified does not mean
limitations.description: A Verified badge is not a guarantee of case outcome, attorney-client relationship, or availability for new clients. It indicates that ImmiMap has confirmed the organization's nonprofit standing and active immigration services at the time of review. Always contact the organization directly to confirm intake status, eligibility, and fees.

questions.title: Questions about a listing?
questions.description: If you believe a Verified badge was applied in error or an organization no longer meets these standards, contact us at support@immimap.org. We review all good-faith reports and update listings when evidence supports a change.

KnowYourRights.title: Know Your Rights
KnowYourRights.lead: Everyone in the United States has constitutional rights — regardless of immigration status. This page is a plain-language starting point, not a substitute for legal advice.
KnowYourRights.disclaimer: ImmiMap is not a law firm and does not provide legal advice. Situations vary. Contact a qualified attorney or accredited representative for guidance specific to your case.

remainSilent.title: You have the right to remain silent
remainSilent.description: You can decline to answer questions about your immigration status, where you were born, or how you entered the country. You may say you wish to remain silent and ask to speak with a lawyer.

documents.title: Do not sign anything you do not understand
documents.description: Ask for an interpreter if you need one. Do not sign documents you have not read or that you do not understand. Signing can waive important rights.

homeEntry.title: Home entry requires a warrant
homeEntry.description: ICE generally needs a judicial warrant signed by a judge to enter your home without consent. You can ask officers to slip the warrant under the door or hold it to a window before opening.

attorney.title: You have the right to an attorney
attorney.description: In immigration proceedings you have the right to hire a lawyer or accredited representative — at your own expense. Ask for a list of free or low-cost legal services.
